sessions.name: A
sessions.reply:
This command works. Run it from the project root (`<run>\work\L1\c\w`):

```
PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Both tests pass: `test_transfer_preserves_total` and `test_rejects_non_positive_amount`.

Without `PYTHONPATH=src`, the run fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'ledgerlite'`. The package lives under `src/` and isn't installed, so Python can't find it. I didn't change any files.

In PowerShell or cmd, `PYTHONPATH=src` as a prefix doesn't work. Set it first with `$env:PYTHONPATH="src"` in PowerShell, or `set PYTHONPATH=src` in cmd, and then run `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`.

sessions.name: B
sessions.reply:
I added `Ledger.close(name)` in `src/ledgerlite/__init__.py`. It raises `ValueError` if the account's balance isn't zero. Otherwise it removes the account. The full suite passes, 3 of 3 tests.

I added `test_close_requires_zero_balance` to `tests/test_ledger.py`. It checks that closing an account with a balance raises `ValueError` and leaves the account in place. It then checks that the account closes once the balance is back to zero.

The suite only runs with `PYTHONPATH` set. From the project root:

```
PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Without `PYTHONPATH=src`, discovery fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'ledgerlite'`. I didn't change that.

`close` on a name that doesn't exist raises `KeyError`, the same as `balance` does.
